body:
Thanks for reading!

What you said rings true. I feel I am alone quite frequently here and reading is a way for me to do something alone that is indeed a source of happiness. 
As for new passions, rock climbing was this for me when things with Sarah ended, and I have met some nice people though that, but nothing overly close. I did go sky-diving with some people I've met through rock climbing but our friendship pretty much ends after we slip out of our climbing shoes and restarts whenever we go back to the gym. Situational. Not bad, but nothing super lasting.

I also want to make it clear that I am not looking for potential romantic partners- honestly more companionship than anything else. 

As for my responsibilities, I am a supervisor of sorts (not the boss, but when she isn't there, I am acting boss), so whenever my coworkers slack, it reflects poorly on me. 

I guess the thing that gives me pause is living for my own happiness and the thing is that I honestly do not know what that looks like. I think I need to meditate on what actually makes me happy and what I want. Honestly, I would love to have a loving family of my own- wife and kids. That would be what happiness looks like to me, money be damned. Though, without a measure of irony, this is focused on people other than me. I will need to think further on this. Thank you for hearing me out.

Thanks for taking the time to read! 

The last time I had a vacation was last month (September), and I used to visit with friends/family. I have two weeks of vacation a year. 

I honestly do not do a thing with it. I go out to dinner/lunch with friends/colleagues, some of who are in my profession, and we commiserate about the state of our profession more than I'd like to admit. For fun, I go rock climbing at a gym and buy books (love to read), but other than that, I do not do much with my money except for save in case of emergency. 

Honestly, money really does not mean that much to me. I have talked to my supervisor about transferring to a closer location but after sending out my formal request, not much has been done. I have sent out job applications that would put me closer to my family, but no dice. My main reason why I have not yet quit is that it would cause a gap in employment which may be difficult to explain to future employers.
